title: Character Frequency in a String
description: Given a string containing no spaces, count the frequency of each character. Print each character and its frequency on a separate line, in the order of its first appearance. Uppercase and lowercase letters must be treated as different characters.
inputFormat: A single line containing a string without spaces.
outputFormat: Print each unique character and its frequency separated by a space on a separate line, in the order of its first appearance in the string.
constraints:
1 <= length of string <= 10^5
The string contains only uppercase and lowercase English letters.

sampleTestCases.explanation: 'b' appears 1 time, 'a' appears 3 times, 'n' appears 2 times. They are printed in order of their first appearance: b, a, n.

sampleTestCases.expectedOutput:
M 2
i 2
n 1
d 1
a 1
t 1
r 1
x 1
sampleTestCases.explanation: 'M' appears 2 times (indices 0 and 4), 'i' appears 2 times, etc. Case sensitive.

hiddenTestCases.expectedOutput:
p 1
r 2
o 1
g 2
a 1
m 2
i 1
n 1

C 2
o 2
d 2
e 2
A 2
r 2
n 2
a 2

title: Second Largest Distinct Element
description: Given an array of N integers, find the second-largest distinct element. If the array does not contain a second-largest distinct element, print -1.
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N representing the size of the array.
Second line contains N space-separated integers.
outputFormat: Print the second-largest distinct element. If no such element exists, print -1.

sampleTestCases.explanation: Distinct elements are 20, 10, 8, 5. The largest is 20, so the second largest is 10.
All elements are identical (7). There is no second distinct largest element, so output -1.

title: Armstrong Number
description:
Given a non-negative integer N, determine whether it is an Armstrong number. An Armstrong number is a number that is equal to the sum of its digits, each raised to the power of the total number of digits.

For example, 153 has 3 digits, and 1^3 + 5^3 + 3^3 = 1 + 125 + 27 = 153.

Print YES if N is an Armstrong number, otherwise print NO.
inputFormat: A single line containing non-negative integer N.
outputFormat: Print YES if N is an Armstrong number, otherwise print NO.

sampleTestCases.explanation: 153 has 3 digits: 1^3 + 5^3 + 3^3 = 1 + 125 + 27 = 153. Hence, it is an Armstrong number.

title: Pyramid Star Pattern
description:
Given an integer N, print a centered pyramid containing N rows. Each row must contain leading spaces followed by an odd number of stars, increasing by two stars in each successive row.

Row 1 has (N - 1) spaces and 1 star.
Row i has (N - i) spaces and (2*i - 1) stars.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer N.
outputFormat: Print the pyramid pattern of N rows.

sampleTestCases.explanation: Row 1 has 3 spaces and 1 star. Row 2 has 2 spaces and 3 stars. Row 3 has 1 space and 5 stars. Row 4 has 0 spaces and 7 stars.
Only 1 row with 0 spaces and 1 star.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
description:
You are given an array of stock prices for N consecutive days. Each element represents the stock price on that day.

Find the maximum profit possible by buying the stock on one day and selling it on a later day. You may complete at most one transaction. If no positive profit is possible, print 0.
inputFormat:
First line contains an integer N, the number of days.
Second line contains N space-separated integers representing stock prices.
outputFormat: Print a single integer representing the maximum profit possible.

sampleTestCases.explanation: Buy on day 2 (price = 1) and sell on day 5 (price = 6), profit = 6 - 1 = 5. Note that buying on day 2 and selling on day 1 is not allowed because you must buy before you sell.
In this case, no transaction is done, i.e. max profit = 0 because the price decreases every day.

title: Product of Array Except Self
description:
Given an array of N integers, construct an output array where each element at index i is equal to the product of all elements in the original array except the element at that index.

You must solve the problem without using division. Assume all required products fit within a signed 64-bit integer.
inputFormat:
First line contains integer N.
Second line contains N space-separated integers.
outputFormat: Print the N space-separated product values on a single line.

sampleTestCases.explanation:
At index 0: 2*3*4 = 24
At index 1: 1*3*4 = 12
At index 2: 1*2*4 = 8
At index 3: 1*2*3 = 6
At index 2, product of other elements is (-1)*1*(-3)*3 = 9. For all other indices, the product includes 0, so they are 0.
